summary:
The Legend of Om - is an interactive, story-driven web application that transforms NASA Earth observation data into a captivating musical and visual experience. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge: Earth Information Jukebox, the project explores how our planet's natural phenomena can be experienced through sound.

The experience follows a fictional Traveller–Musician who discovers that Earth's oceans and lightning storms contain patterns that can be interpreted musically. Through cinematic illustrations, interactive narration, and original soundscapes, users explore how ocean-current visualizations inspire flute melodies and lightning observations inspire electric guitar compositions.

By combining environmental data visualization with sonification—the process of translating data into sound—the project makes complex Earth science more approachable, engaging, and memorable.

Unlike conventional data dashboards, The Legend of Om presents scientific information through an interactive adventure where users progress through illustrated scenes, discover musical interpretations, and learn about NASA's Earth observations.

Our goal is to make Earth science accessible to wider audiences by connecting scientific curiosity, storytelling, art, and music.

The Legend of Om — Project Details

Project Overview

The Legend of Om is an interactive cinematic storytelling application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Earth Information Jukebox challenge.

The project explores an imaginative question: What if Earth itself were the greatest musician, and we could translate its natural patterns into music?

Our application combines NASA Earth observation visualizations, data-inspired musical compositions, interactive storytelling, and cinematic artwork to create an educational experience that allows users to discover the hidden rhythms of our planet.

How Does It Work?

The application follows a Traveller–Musician on a journey to discover the music of nature. The experience is divided into six interconnected chapters.

Chapter 1 — The Call of the Wind

The traveller discovers mysterious sounds carried by the wind and begins searching for their origin.

Chapter 2 — The Ocean Shoreline

At the coastline, the traveller encounters the natural rhythms of wind and waves, inspiring him to explore how environmental patterns might be represented through music.

Chapter 3 — The Ocean Symphony

Inspired by NASA ocean-current visualizations, the traveller creates a wooden flute. Ocean circulation patterns are artistically interpreted as melodic variations, introducing users to the concept of sonification.

The application illustrates how properties extracted from environmental data can be mapped to musical characteristics such as pitch, tempo, and melodic movement.

Chapter 4 — The Arrival of the Storm

The traveller encounters a powerful lightning storm, revealing an entirely different natural rhythm.

Chapter 5 — The Lightning Symphony

The traveller constructs an electric guitar and explores how lightning observations can inspire musical compositions.

Lightning activity is represented through energetic guitar sounds, with variations in the observed patterns influencing the musical interpretation.

The traveller also creates maps to illustrate geographical variations in environmental activity.

Chapter 6 — The Earth Jukebox

The journey concludes with an Earth Jukebox that brings the ocean-inspired flute and lightning-inspired guitar compositions together.

Users discover how different environmental phenomena can produce distinct musical interpretations, demonstrating the relationship between scientific observations and sound.

Interactive Web Application

Rather than presenting scientific data through conventional charts alone, our project introduces an interactive storytelling experience.

Users begin by opening a traditional parchment scroll sealed with wax, entering the world of The Legend of Ohm.

The experience includes:

  • Interactive storytelling: Users progress through individual cinematic frames and chapters.
  • Illustrated narrator: A dedicated narrator character guides users through the story and explains scientific concepts.
  • Audio experiences: Musical soundscapes accompany the ocean and lightning chapters.
  • Environmental visualizations: NASA-inspired imagery illustrates ocean currents and lightning activity.
  • Educational explanations: Scientific concepts are introduced naturally during the traveller's discoveries.
  • Cinematic presentation: Painterly, cel-shaded illustrations, atmospheric lighting, and subtle transitions create an immersive experience.

NASA Data and Sonification

The project draws inspiration from NASA's Earth Information Center visualizations, particularly ocean circulation and lightning activity.

These two environmental phenomena were selected because they offer contrasting musical characteristics.

Ocean Currents — Flute Sonification

Ocean circulation is represented through flowing melodies. Changes in visualized environmental patterns can be interpreted through musical parameters such as pitch, note duration, and melodic progression.

The flute represents the smooth and continuous movement of ocean currents.

Lightning — Electric Guitar Sonification

Lightning activity is represented through energetic guitar compositions. Variations in the observed lightning patterns can be translated into changes in musical intensity, rhythm, and pitch.

The electric guitar symbolizes the sudden, powerful, and irregular nature of lightning events.

These sonifications are artistic interpretations of environmental observations rather than recordings of physical sounds emitted by the datasets.

Technologies and Tools

The application is designed as a lightweight, browser-based experience using accessible web technologies.

Frontend Development

  • HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript
  • Responsive web design
  • Interactive frame navigation and scene transitions
  • Browser-based audio playback and narration

Deployment

  • Netlify for free static website hosting
  • Git and GitHub for version control and project management, where applicable

Creative Production

  • AI-assisted character and storyboard illustration
  • Digital audio editing and soundscape preparation
  • Custom environmental data-inspired musical arrangements

Scientific Resources

  • NASA Earth Information Center visualizations
  • Ocean-current visualization imagery
  • Lightning observation visualizations

The project is designed to operate without paid APIs or specialized hardware, making it practical to host and share online.

Creativity and Innovation

The primary innovation of The Legend of Ohm is its combination of scientific data interpretation with character-driven storytelling.

Instead of requiring users to understand complex scientific charts before engaging with Earth observation data, the project introduces these concepts through a fictional musician's discoveries.

The two environmental phenomena are assigned contrasting instruments, creating a recognizable relationship between natural patterns and musical expression.

The project also uses an illustrated narrator, a parchment-scroll introduction, hand-drawn maps, and cinematic transitions to make scientific exploration feel like an unfolding adventure.

This approach combines science, technology, storytelling, visual art, and music in a single interactive experience.

Design Considerations

During development, our team prioritized scientific clarity, visual consistency, accessibility, storytelling, and performance.

We aimed to preserve the distinction between observed environmental data and the artistic decisions used to represent that data musically.

We also focused on creating an experience that can run directly in a web browser, without requiring users to install specialized software.

Conclusion

The Legend of Om transforms Earth observation into an interactive musical adventure.

By connecting NASA environmental visualizations with sound, storytelling, and cinematic artwork, the project demonstrates a creative way to communicate Earth science.

Our vision is to help audiences experience the planet not only as something to observe, but also as something to listen to, interpret, and understand.

The Earth has patterns. We turn them into music.
